# Template built from HTTP request data (Node.js)

`qualor:js/template-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-1336](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1336.html), [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data used as a template (Express, Fastify, Next.js):

- the template source given to EJS `render()`/`compile()`, Pug `render()`/`compile()`,
  Handlebars `compile()`/`precompile()`, Nunjucks `renderString()`/`compile()` and lodash
  `template()`;
- EJS options taken from the request;
- for EJS, a request object passed whole as the data of a render
  (`res.render('index', req.query)`), from which EJS also reads render options.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
Template engines compile templates into JavaScript. EJS and lodash `template()` run any code
between their tags, and the others offer ways out of their expressions too. A client who writes
the template text can therefore run code on the server or read its data; with EJS, request data
passed whole as render data can set options that change how the template is compiled.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the name is pasted into the template text.

```javascript
const express = require('express');
const ejs = require('ejs');

const app = express();

app.get('/hello', (req, res) => {
  const html = ejs.render('<p>Hello, ' + req.query.name + '</p>');
  res.send(html);
});
```

**Compliant:** the template is a fixed file; the name is a value in the data object, and EJS
escapes it with `<%= name %>`.

```javascript
const express = require('express');

const app = express();
app.set('view engine', 'ejs');

app.get('/hello', (req, res) => {
  res.render('hello', { name: req.query.name });
});
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep templates fixed (files or constants) and pass request data as values in a data object:
  `res.render('view', { q: req.query.q })`.
- Never pass a request object whole as render data: copy the fields you need.
- If users choose between templates, pick one from an allow-list.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Express
- Next.js
- Fastify
- EJS
- Pug
- Handlebars
- Nunjucks
- Lodash

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A request object passed whole to `res.render()` is reported only when EJS is visibly the engine
  (a view name ending in `.ejs`, or `app.set('view engine', 'ejs')` / `app.engine(..., ejs.renderFile)`
  in the same file), and only when it is passed or spread in place, not through a variable.
- With `app.engine('html', ejs.renderFile)` next to another default engine, views rendered by the
  other engine are reported too.
- An allow-list lookup is recognised only in a `const` table with literal keys and values in the
  same file.
- Request handlers are recognised by the name of their second parameter (`res`, `reply`, `ctx`,
  `next`, ...): a handler written as `(request, out)` is not checked.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test files [`rules/js/template/template-injection.js`](../../../rules/js/template/template-injection.js) and [`rules/js/template/template-injection.ts`](../../../rules/js/template/template-injection.ts) hold every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.
